description: 4Fe-4S iron-sulfur cluster parameters covering HiPIP and ferredoxin redox couples. 15 per-guess parameter sets (one per broken-symmetry initial guess) plus 3 averaged sets (one per redox state, multi-conformer + group-equivalence RESP + arithmetic-mean Seminario across BS guesses). Each per-guess set has a unique cluster residue code and 4 unique modified-cysteinate residues so multiple clusters can coexist. Averaged sets use FO0/FR0/FD0 cluster residues and CXO/CXR/CXD shared ligand residues.
references: Parameters derived from B3LYP/6-31G(d,p)+GD3 / C-PCM (diethyl ether, eps=4) DFT calculations followed by MCPB.py Seminario method (bonded) and 2-stage RESP charge fitting on an ACE-CYS-NME large protein-cap model with ff14SB CYM backbone constraints.
Fe MK ESP radii chosen as the IOD-weighted average of Li-Merz Fe(II)/Fe(III) Rmin/2 values per oxidation state.

Guberman_FO0_RESP.name: Averaged Oxidized HiPIP [Fe4S4]³⁺ (6-BS-guess mean)
Guberman_FO0_RESP.methodology: Averaged across BS guesses. BOND/ANGL force constants are the arithmetic mean of the Seminario values from each per-guess MCPB fit, after collapsing all 4 Fe (resp. 4 bridging S, 4 Cys SG) to a single atom type. Charges from the standard two-stage RESP procedure — the same protocol as the per-guess sets (stage 1 free fit, qwt=0.0005; stage 2 methylene HB2=HB3 equivalenced with heavy atoms frozen, qwt=0.0010) — run jointly over the combined ESP grid of all BS guesses, with the 4 Fe / 4 bridging S / 4 Cys SG each equivalenced to a single charge across all conformers. The two methylene protons therefore share one charge (2026-07 correction: the original deposit used a non-standard single-stage fit that left HB2≠HB3). Fe LJ is composition-weighted (0.75 Fe³⁺ + 0.25 Fe²⁺; Rmin/2 = 1.3917 Å, ε = 0.01448 kcal/mol) between Li-Song-Merz Fe³⁺ (1.386 / 0.01357) and Li-Roberts-Chakravorty-Merz Fe²⁺ (1.409 / 0.01721) TIP3P IOD values. Use for studies of integer redox-state changes where BS-specific asymmetry is not required (charge capacitance, pKa coupling, redox-driven ET). For BS-specific work, pick a per-guess set instead.

transforms_from: PDB 4Fe-4S cluster residue (e.g. SF4, FES, F3S) with atoms FE1 FE2 FE3 FE4 S1 S2 S3 S4
4 CYS residues whose SG atoms ligate the 4 Fe centers (~2.3 A)
creates_bonds: 12 internal cubane Fe-S bonds within the cluster residue
4 inter-residue Fe-SG bonds linking the cluster to its modified cysteinate ligands
transformation_info.notes: Cys-Fe matching is deterministic: for each FE<n> atom, the closest CYS SG becomes the n-th modified cysteinate (e.g. FO1: FE1->C01, FE2->C02, FE3->C03, FE4->C04). Both .frcmod (loadamberparams) and .lib (loadoff) must be loaded for the chosen set; the .frcmod must be loaded before the .lib so that the state-letter atom types are defined.

methodology:
Cluster model. Two computational models per the MCPB.py workflow. The small model truncates each of the 4 cysteinate ligands at C-alpha (saturating with H) for Seminario bonded-parameter input; total atom count 40. The large model extends each cysteine to an ACE-CYS-NME tripeptide cap with ff14SB backbone geometry frozen at protein-derived coordinates, used for RESP charge fitting. The backbone constraint preserves the protein-imposed alpha-carbon position while letting the side chain and cluster relax.

DFT method. B3LYP with Grimme D3 dispersion, 6-31G(d,p) basis, C-PCM solvation in diethyl ether (ε=4) as a protein-dielectric mimic. Ultrafine integration grid; tight SCF with quadratic-convergence backup; symmetry disabled; unrestricted formalism for the broken-symmetry states.

Broken-symmetry treatment. Three distinct ways to pair the 4 Fe atoms into ferric and mixed-valence groupings yield 6 spin-coupling guesses for the oxidized and reduced-ferredoxin states, 3 guesses for the reduced-HiPIP state (alpha/beta variants collapse when the two mixed-valence layers are equivalent). Each guess is a distinct initial-density seed; the optimizer converges to that guess's specific BS solution.

10-step calculation pipeline. Initial high-spin geometry optimization, SCF stability check, re-opt from the stable density, BS initial-guess generation, BS opt, post-opt stability check, frequency calculation (Hessian), Merz-Kollman ESP single-point. Steps 1-4 are shared across guesses; steps 5-10 are per-guess. Where the constrained small-model geometry yields one or two small imaginary frequencies (-5 to -30 cm⁻¹) as artifacts of the alpha-carbon constraint, the geometry is displaced 0.2 Å along the imaginary mode and re-optimized until the Hessian passes.

Bonded parameters. Seminario method on the diagonal blocks of the Cartesian Hessian from the small-model Step 9 frequency calculation, via pymsmt (the MCPB.py back-end shipped with AmberTools 22).

RESP charges. Standard two-stage Bayly-Cieplak-Cornell-Kollman procedure. ff14SB CYM backbone atoms (N, HN, CA, HA, C, O) are constrained to their canonical charges in the RESP fit so the resulting modified-cysteinate residues integrate seamlessly with the rest of CYM in MD simulations. The three averaged sets (FD0/FO0/FR0) apply this same two-stage procedure jointly across all BS-guess ESP grids, additionally equivalencing the 4 Fe / 4 bridging S / 4 Cys SG to a single charge each across conformers; the methylene HB2/HB3 remain equivalenced by stage 2, and the per-atom-name mean over the 4 cysteines yields the shared CXO/CXR/CXD ligand residue. (A 2026-07 rebuild switched the averaged sets from an earlier non-standard single-stage fit, which had left HB2≠HB3, to this two-stage joint fit; validated by reproducing the per-guess resp2 charges to 1e-6 with the cross-conformer equivalencing disabled.)

Fe MK ESP radius. Linear interpolation between Li-Merz Fe(II) (Rmin/2 = 1.409 Å, JCTC 2013, 9, 2733) and Fe(III) (Rmin/2 = 1.386 Å, JPCB 2015, 119, 883) IOD-set values, weighted by the formal oxidation-state composition of each cluster: 1.392 Å for oxidized [Fe4S4]³⁺ (3 Fe³⁺ + 1 Fe²⁺), 1.398 Å for reduced HiPIP [Fe4S4]²⁺ (2 Fe³⁺ + 2 Fe²⁺), 1.403 Å for reduced ferredoxin [Fe4S4]⁺ (1 Fe³⁺ + 3 Fe²⁺). These are LJ Rmin/2 parameters used as a proxy for the MK ESP radius (no canonical literature MK ESP radius exists for Fe).

Validation. All 10 calculation steps terminate normally per state; Mulliken spin populations on the 4 Fe atoms match the intended BS coupling pattern (magnitudes ~±4.0 for oxidized, ~±3.85 for reduced HiPIP, ~±3.8 for reduced Fd); total RESP charge sums to the cluster's overall formal charge (-1, -2, or -3).
set_comparison_guidance:
The 15 parameter sets span three redox states with multiple broken-symmetry initial-guess starting points per state — 6 for oxidized [Fe4S4]³⁺, 3 for reduced HiPIP [Fe4S4]²⁺, and 6 for reduced ferredoxin [Fe4S4]⁺. Each guess corresponds to a specific spin-coupling pattern among the 4 Fe atoms.

Spin patterns are shown as the sign sequence (Fe1, Fe2, Fe3, Fe4) with + for majority-alpha and − for majority-beta spin density. The three ways to partition the 4 Fe atoms into ferric and mixed-valence pairs are 'guess 1' ({Fe1,Fe2}|{Fe3,Fe4}), 'guess 2' ({Fe1,Fe3}|{Fe2,Fe4}), and 'guess 3' ({Fe1,Fe4}|{Fe2,Fe3}). Where applicable, alpha/beta variants (a/b) capture the two orientations of the spin density on the mixed-valence pair.

Different guesses yield qualitatively similar parameter values but differ in detail because the specific ferric/mixed-valence partition affects the local electronic structure on each Fe. The standard practice is to pick the guess whose spin-coupling pattern best matches the experimentally determined pattern for the cluster in the protein of interest (typically from EPR, or by following the convention established for a closely related protein). If no pattern is known a priori, the convention is to use the lowest-energy converged BS state (default: FO1 / FR1 / FD1).
